definition: Aspersion means a remark meant to damage someone's reputation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word aspersion. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know aspersion should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: One aspersion in a trade paper — 'convenient bookkeeping' — cost the firm two clients by Friday.
A dig is far gentler than an aspersion — a little elbow in conversation that stings for a minute and draws no blood, while an aspersion is aimed squarely at a reputation and leaves a mark there.
Slander goes further than an aspersion — an aspersion plants a doubt; slander states a false, damaging fact outright, the kind courts get involved in.

A smear is the blunt journalistic word for a reputation attack, and it usually names the whole coordinated effort — a smear campaign of planted stories and repetition. An aspersion is a single remark inside that kind of effort: one insinuation cast, one doubt left where a reputation used to be solid.

A slur is a one-word insult thrown openly to wound, and everyone in the room hears it as an attack. An aspersion works more quietly: it insinuates something to be doubted, so listeners do the suspecting themselves. The slur strikes in the open; the aspersion stains from the side.

Lena's water-purity sensor won the regional science fair on a Saturday; by Monday, half the school doubted she had built it.
The trouble began with one sentence.

As the judges pinned the ribbon, a rival's parent said, just loudly enough, 'Her uncle does work at the county lab, you know.' It was an aspersion, not an accusation — nothing anyone could rebut, only a seed of suspicion left to sprout on its own.
Students repeated it; a teacher hesitated before congratulating her; the fair's committee quietly requested her notebooks.
The notebooks showed eleven months of dated entries, and the committee apologized.
The parent had never said Lena cheated — and had never needed to.
